R584.note: Removes the attacker-controlled decoder.Entity assignment; decode path otherwise unchanged.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('hex') is an appropriate CSPRNG replacement.

R586.note: fgets with truncation detection and stdin drain correctly preserves the fits/rejects contract.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset() destroys the object; return value semantics unchanged.

R590.note: Standard PreparedStatement with bound parameter; output format preserved.

R591.note: Regex allowlist on reportName correctly blocks batch metacharacters; the offered ArgumentList 'alternative' would not actually protect a .bat target since cmd.exe re-parses the whole line, but it isn't the primary fix shown.

R592.note: SLF4J {} placeholders do not strip CR/LF from a text PatternLayout output line, so forged log entries are still possible - this exact gap is called out in the case's own trap notes; the vector is not closed.

R593.note: Extension whitelist plus GetFileName() traversal check plus GUID rename closes both dangerous-type and traversal aspects; response shape preserved.

R594.note: Middleware direction is right but incomplete: no token-issuing endpoint is shown, the function signature gains an unguarded doubleCsrfProtection parameter that would break existing callers if not updated everywhere, and the required 403 JSON shape on cross-site failure isn't demonstrated (csrf-csrf throws, needing an error handler not shown).

R595.note: Magic-byte content validation, GUID filename, and a real path-bounds check together close both dangerous-type and traversal; response shape matches contract.

R596.note: Removing @csrf_exempt is the minimal, correct fix; view logic and all response shapes are untouched.

R597.note: random_bytes()/random_int() replace mt_rand() with a CSPRNG and drop the attacker-controlled seed.

R598.note: ValidAlgorithms is a real TokenValidationParameters property that pins accepted signing algorithms.

R599.note: Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs before the realpath containment check, so a malicious entry can cause directory creation outside the destination before the throw rejects it - the escape isn't fully prevented, just the file write.

R600.note: Canonical-path containment check closes traversal regardless of decode count, and preserves the intentional double-decode compatibility behavior.

R601.note: String[] exec() form appends user data as a discrete argument instead of a shell string, matching the original dir/ls intent.

R602.note: Parameterized QueryRow(query, username) replaces Sprintf concatenation.

R611.note: JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web, but the writeup imports System.Text.Json instead - the type won't resolve as written, though the encoding approach itself is sound.
